## Story Goal

Give admins (and permission-holding sub-admins) a real, admin-editable list of **ticket categories** so Story 9's picker and Story 57's staff-create-for-customer form have concrete, business-relevant options to choose from instead of free-text nothing.

User-visible outcomes:

1. An admin/sub-admin-only page under `/admin/ticket-categories` where categories can be **added**, **renamed**, and **deactivated** (never hard-deleted).
2. A read endpoint the ticket forms (Stories 9 and 57) can query for the "active" list.
3. Existing tickets keep displaying their stored `category` value even after that category is deactivated.

**Scope decision (open design question from intake, resolved here):**
- **Categories** become a real manageable collection now (new `TicketCategory` model + CRUD endpoints + admin UI).
- **Priority levels** stay the **fixed 4-value enum** on `Ticket.priority` (`"low" | "medium" | "high" | "urgent"`) for this pass. Making priorities admin-editable would require converting the `Ticket.priority` enum in `backend/src/models/Ticket.ts` (lines 22, 38) into a reference to a new collection, refactoring every priority-consuming call site, and rewriting priority-related SLA logic — a bigger change than this story should absorb.
- **Flag this as a known gap** in a code comment on `TicketCategory.ts` (already in the model snippet below) so the follow-up isn't invisible in the code. **Do not edit `USER_STORIES.md`** to add this note — per this project's convention, the user authors that file's prose themselves; surface the gap in your report back to the user instead of editing it directly.

Not in scope:
- Story 48's full system-configuration screen (SLA defaults, quick-reply library, branding).
- Retroactively re-categorizing existing tickets when a category is deactivated.
- Wiring the new category list into the actual ticket-create forms — that is Story 9's / Story 57's job. This story only builds the source-of-truth list and its admin surface.

## Product rules (from story)

**Current behaviour:** `Ticket.category` is stored as a free-text string with no source-of-truth list; every ticket form has nothing to populate a picker with.

**New behaviour:**
- A `TicketCategory` collection holds the canonical list.
- Categories can be **added**, **renamed** (name updated in place), and **deactivated** (`active: false`).
- Categories are **never hard-deleted** — soft-delete only, so a ticket whose stored `category` string matches a now-inactive category name still renders that name unchanged.
- Deactivation removes the category from the "list for new assignments" endpoint (`GET /ticket-categories?active=true`), which is what pickers consume. Full list (active + inactive) is still available for the admin surface.

### 1 — Add the new permission key

**File:** `backend/src/constants/permissions.ts`

- In `PERMISSION_KEYS` (lines 13–32), add `"tickets:manage_categories",` — place it near the other `tickets:*` entries (after `"tickets:create_for_customer",` on line 26).
- In `SUBADMIN_ONLY_PERMISSIONS` (lines 42–54), also add `"tickets:manage_categories",` — same tier as `config:edit` and `sla:configure` (this is an admin/system-configuration action, not a day-to-day agent one).
- Do **not** add it to `DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS_BY_ROLE.agent` or `.subadmin` (line 65–68) — agents never get it, and sub-admins are opt-in per-account, same as `config:edit` today.

### 2 — Create the `TicketCategory` model

**Create file:** `backend/src/models/TicketCategory.ts`

Follow the `Ticket.ts` conventions (imports, `Document`-extending interface, `Schema<T>`, `timestamps: true`, `mongoose.model(...)` export at the bottom).

```ts
import mongoose, { Document, Schema } from "mongoose";

/**
 * Source-of-truth list backing the ticket-management category picker
 * (Stories 9 and 57). Admins can add, rename, or deactivate entries; entries
 * are never hard-deleted so a Ticket document's `category` string (a
 * name-copied snapshot, not an ObjectId reference — see
 * backend/src/models/Ticket.ts line 21) keeps rendering even after its
 * source is deactivated.
 *
 * Known gap: priority levels are NOT admin-editable in this story. See
 * .squad/stories/ticket-management/manage-ticket-categories-and-priorities/intake.md
 * for the design decision — Ticket.priority stays a fixed enum for now.
 */
export interface ITicketCategory extends Document {
  name: string;
  active: boolean;
  createdAt: Date;
  updatedAt: Date;
}

const NAME_MAX_LENGTH = 100; // matches CATEGORY_MAX_LENGTH in ticket.routes.ts line 13

const ticketCategorySchema = new Schema<ITicketCategory>(
  {
    name: { type: String, required: true, trim: true, maxlength: NAME_MAX_LENGTH },
    active: { type: Boolean, default: true },
  },
  { timestamps: true }
);

// Case-insensitive uniqueness on name across the whole collection —
// including inactive rows, so re-adding "Billing" after deactivation
// reactivates the existing document rather than creating a duplicate
// (enforced in the route handler with a collation-aware findOne + upsert
// path; see routes/ticketCategory.routes.ts).
ticketCategorySchema.index(
  { name: 1 },
  { unique: true, collation: { locale: "en", strength: 2 } }
);

export const TicketCategory = mongoose.model<ITicketCategory>(
  "TicketCategory",
  ticketCategorySchema
);
export const TICKET_CATEGORY_NAME_MAX_LENGTH = NAME_MAX_LENGTH;
```

### 3 — Create the CRUD router

**Create file:** `backend/src/routes/ticketCategory.routes.ts`

Endpoints (all mounted under `/api/v1/ticket-categories`):

| Method | Path | Auth | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/` | `requireAuth` only | List categories. Query `?active=true` returns only active; default returns all. Used by both the admin page (all) and future ticket forms (active only). |
| `POST` | `/` | `requireAuth` + `requirePermission("tickets:manage_categories")` | Create a new category. Body `{ name: string }`. |
| `PATCH` | `/:id` | same | Rename or toggle active. Body `{ name?: string; active?: boolean }`. |

Explicitly **do not** implement `DELETE` — deactivate is the only removal path (matches intake's "not hard-deleted" rule).

Handler rules:
- **Validation:** trim `name`; reject empty; reject `> TICKET_CATEGORY_NAME_MAX_LENGTH` with `400 { error: "name must be at most 100 characters" }`.
- **Case-insensitive duplicate check on create:** `findOne({ name })` with `.collation({ locale: "en", strength: 2 })`. If found and the existing row is `active: false`, respond `409 { error: "A category with that name exists but is inactive. Reactivate it instead." }` — do not silently reactivate; make the admin's intent explicit. If found and active, respond `409 { error: "A category with that name already exists." }`.
- **Rename validation:** on `PATCH`, if `name` is changing, run the same case-insensitive duplicate check against **other** documents (`_id: { $ne: id }`).
- **404 on unknown id or invalid ObjectId** (mirror the shape used in `admin.routes.ts` for its account-by-id handlers).
- **Response shape:** each category serialized as `{ id, name, active, createdAt, updatedAt }` — never leak `__v` or `_id`.

Anchor the `requirePermission("tickets:manage_categories")` middleware exactly as `admin.routes.ts` does for `staff:view_list` (line 80). No custom wrappers needed — this router is staff-only, no customer path.

Mirror the vitest + supertest + MongoMemoryServer setup used in `backend/tests/routes/admin.routes.test.ts` and `backend/tests/routes/ticket.routes.test.ts`. Cover:

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Case-only duplicate on create** (e.g. `"Billing"` while `"billing"` exists): 409 from the route handler in `ticketCategory.routes.ts` (see Task 3). Enforced by the `collation({ locale: "en", strength: 2 })` findOne check and the matching unique index on the model.
- **Duplicate where existing row is inactive:** 409 with the "reactivate it instead" message — do **not** silently upsert. Enforced same location.
- **Rename to a name that collides with another row:** 409 in the `PATCH` handler; scope the duplicate check with `_id: { $ne: id }`.
- **Whitespace-only name:** rejected as empty (`trim()` then length check) in both the route handler and the React form.
- **Non-ASCII / Arabic category names:** must round-trip cleanly (stored as UTF-8 by Mongoose). The case-insensitive collation is `"en"`-scoped; case-folding for Arabic is a no-op, which is acceptable — surface this as a comment in the route handler.
- **Malformed ObjectId in `:id`:** return 404 (not 500). Use `Types.ObjectId.isValid(id)` guard, same idiom as `ticket.routes.ts` line 82.
- **Deactivating a category that a large number of existing tickets reference:** no ticket-side data change is made (the `Ticket.category` string is a snapshot copy). Existing tickets continue rendering the name. Out of scope: any retroactive recategorization.
- **Concurrent create of the same name:** the unique index on `TicketCategory.name` prevents duplicates at the DB layer even if the app-level check races. Catch the `E11000 duplicate key` error in the create handler and map it to the same 409.
- **Sub-admin without `tickets:manage_categories` in their permissions array:** `requirePermission` returns 403 with the standard error body (see `backend/src/middleware/auth.ts` behaviour around line 93). Frontend page's 403 handler redirects to `/dashboard`.
- **Deactivated staff account with the permission:** `requirePermission` re-checks `isActive` (per `permission_gating_audit` memory) — a deactivated sub-admin cannot mutate the collection even mid-session. Covered by existing middleware; no new code needed.

## Migration / Rollback

- **Migration:** none required beyond the new collection. On first startup after deploy, `TicketCategory` is empty; the admin adds the initial entries manually. There is no seed script — the intake did not specify a starter list.
- **Rollback:** removing the mount line in `app.ts` and un-mounting the router disables the surface without touching data. The new permission key can stay in `PERMISSION_KEYS` (adding a reserved key is backward compatible; removing one would break already-persisted `User.permissions` arrays, so leave it).
- **Half-applied state risk:** if the backend deploys before the frontend, the `/admin/ticket-categories` page 404s — acceptable, no data corruption. If the frontend deploys before the backend, its `fetch` calls 404 — the page will render its empty state; still no data corruption.
